title: A Garden for the Ember
premise: Freya Reyes has survived five years in the city of Vell by hiding the ember-glow of their magic behind charms and silence, but when King Aldric declares a purge of the gifted, Freya's old mentor is taken and Freya discovers the truth: the king died years ago, and a parasitic spirit called the Hollow Crown now rules through his body, feeding on the gift of every witch it burns. To save their mentor and the city's hidden magical community, Freya must ally with a disgraced royal gardener who knows the palace's oldest secret—a garden planted over the wellspring where the Crown was first bound. In the climax, Freya offers their own ember to rebind the spirit, but instead of being consumed, they learn that power freely shared cannot be corrupted; they unmake the Crown, free the king's lingering ghost to rest, and choose at last to belong—to the city, to the garden, and to themselves.
about_author: Theo Winterbourne is the pen name of a former botanist who traded greenhouse benches for manuscript pages after a decade cataloguing rare plants in coastal fog country. Their fiction grows from a lifelong fascination with gardens as places where memory, power, and patience take root.

chapters.title: Charms for Small Coin
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the market quarter of Vell, Freya sells luck-knots and fever-charms while hiding their gift beneath iron-thread gloves. A child customer's charm flares visible light, drawing a warden's attention. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life half-lived, and the first crack in Freya's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Criers announce the king's edict: all gifted persons must register or be burned. Freya races to warn their former mentor, Maren, only to find her cottage already ransacked and her apprentice mark left deliberately behind—a message. Emotional beat: fear curdling into guilt; running was never the same as being safe.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with a brief interlude from warden Captain Ilsa Voss. Following Maren's trail, Freya witnesses a public 'cleansing' and sees the king up close—recognizing the wrongness in him: no breath-fog in cold air, shadows moving against the light. Emotional beat: horror and dawning understanding that this is not cruelty but hunger.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Gate
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Hunted through the palace outskirts, Freya is pulled to safety by Tam, a disgraced royal gardener who once served the true king. He reveals the garden was planted as a seal over the wellspring where the Hollow Crown was first bound—and that it is dying. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two people who have both survived by keeping their heads down.

chapters.title: Roots and Ashes
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam shows Freya the garden's failing heart-tree and recounts the night he fled the palace, when the thing in the crown consumed the queen's gift before his eyes. Freya realizes Maren is being kept alive as bait—or fuel. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve; Tam chooses to stop hiding.

chapters.title: The Registry
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. To reach Maren, Freya infiltrates the registry where confiscated witches are held, using a forged writ from Ilsa Voss's stolen seals. They find Maren weakened but lucid; she warns that the Crown wants an ember-bearer specifically—Freya's rare lineage. Emotional beat: reunion shadowed by revelation; Freya learns they were never invisible, only being saved for last.

chapters.title: A Traitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss's POV. The captain, whose sister burned in the first cleansing, secretly frees Freya and Maren, offering palace access in exchange for ending the king's torment. Betrayed by a double agent among the wardens, the escape collapses. Emotional beat: trust tested and broken; Ilsa's cold duty cracking into open rebellion.

chapters.title: The Well Beneath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Captured and dragged before the Hollow Crown, Freya endures its seduction—it promises belonging, purpose, an end to hiding. Maren breaks the binding circle with the last of her strength; Tam opens the garden gate from within. Emotional beat: the lowest point—Freya nearly surrenders their identity to be told who to be.

chapters.title: Ember and Root
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the dying garden above the wellspring, Freya offers their ember not as sacrifice but as invitation—power freely given, which the Crown cannot digest. The binding reverses; the spirit unravels, and the dead king's ghost, briefly freed, thanks them before dissolving. Emotional beat: triumphant catharsis; corruption fails against something genuinely shared.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Ember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, closing with Ilsa's epilogue letter. Weeks later, magic is decriminalized; Freya plants the heart-tree's cutting in the restored garden and takes apprentices—including the child from chapter one. Maren recovers; Tam stays. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—belonging chosen, not granted; a life fully lit at last.
